participantInstructions: The Business Law and Ethics Team Decision Making Event is presented to you through your reading of the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation. You will have thirty (30) minutes to review the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation to develop your strategy. You will then have up to fifteen (15) minutes to make your presentation to the judge and respond to the judge's questions. Both members of the participant team must take part in the presentation and in answering the judge's questions. You will be evaluated on how well your presentation reflects your ability to meet the performance indicators of this event. All notes and materials are to be turned in to the judge at the end of the event.
situation:
You are to assume the roles of data security coordinator and customer relations coordinator at CROSS RIDGE FREIGHT LINES, a regional trucking carrier that has hauled refrigerated freight across the Midwest under three generations of the same family. The owner (judge) built the company's growth on a network of independent owner-operators rather than company drivers, and has asked you to meet about a security incident that surfaced late last week inside the payroll system that pays those owner-operators.

A vendor that processes weekly settlement payments to roughly one hundred forty owner-operators notified Cross Ridge on Thursday that an outside party had accessed the portal where those drivers submit routing numbers and Social Security numbers for tax reporting. The vendor's own investigation is still narrow, and Cross Ridge does not yet know exactly how many accounts were viewed, only that the exposure window lasted twelve days before anyone noticed the unusual login activity.

IT has confirmed the access point is closed, and legal counsel says state law requires notifying only the owner-operators whose specific records were confirmed viewed, a number counsel currently puts at under twenty. Notifying only that narrow group costs almost nothing and meets the letter of the law, but the vendor cannot yet rule out that its logs are incomplete, and a handful of owner-operators are already comparing notes about unfamiliar charges in a private social media group for the fleet.

The owner (judge) could instead notify the entire roster of owner-operators, pay for credit monitoring, and post an explanation on the company's social media pages before drivers post their own version of events, an approach that would cost far more and openly signal to competing carriers and shipping clients that Cross Ridge had a breach at all. The owner (judge) wants your team's analysis of what the company owes the owner-operators against what broader disclosure would cost the carrier's standing with the shipping clients who trust it with their freight.

Dispatch staff are already fielding calls from confused owner-operators and need direction on what they may say before any official notice goes out, and the customer service team that handles the shipping clients has asked whether this incident should be mentioned to them at all before a client raises it first. The owner (judge) wants a specific recommendation on who is told, when, and through what channel, along with how the company would know afterward whether the choice actually protected the people it was meant to protect.

The owner (judge) will greet you and ask you to present your recommendation for how Cross Ridge should respond to the breach and communicate with those it affects. The owner (judge) will listen to your presentation and then ask you questions about it. At the conclusion of your presentation and the questions that follow, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner of Cross Ridge Freight Lines, the third generation of your family to run the carrier. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked two members of your team to analyze how the company should respond to a security incident affecting the payroll portal used by your owner-operators, and to recommend who should be notified, when, and through what channel, weighing what the owner-operators are owed against what broader disclosure would cost the carrier's standing with its shipping clients.

During the presentation, you will ask the participants the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would we know, a few months from now, whether this was the right call?
What should dispatch tell an owner-operator who calls today, before anything has been decided?
